stories.developer_impact: Developers using OpenSSL must upgrade to the patched version that includes the fix for EVP_EncodeBlock, verify that their build pipelines pull the updated library, and consider auditing any custom code that calls this function for potential exploitation.
stories.headline: OpenSSL fixes critical buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock (CVE-2026-121481)

sources.title: OpenSSL: Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock() (CVE-2026-121481, CVSS 9.8)

stories.what_happened: A buffer overflow vulnerability was identified in OpenSSL's EVP_EncodeBlock() function and assigned CVE-2026-121481 with a CVSS score of 9.8. The issue has been disclosed on Hacker News and a corresponding pull request was opened in the OpenSSL repository to address it.
stories.why_it_matters: The high severity rating indicates the flaw could be exploited for remote code execution or denial‑of‑service attacks in any software that relies on OpenSSL for encoding operations, posing a significant security risk to servers and services worldwide.

stories.headline: LLM coding agents evaluated on deployment-style PHM benchmark NextUnit-Bench

sources.title: Moving Generality from Model to Modeler: LLM Agents for PHM on a Deployment-Style Benchmark

stories.what_happened: Researchers introduced a benchmark called NextUnit-Bench for prognostics and health management (PHM) that includes 24 public datasets split into 58 folds with held‑out units or operating conditions. They used large‑language‑model (LLM) coding agents to automatically generate a model for each new PHM task, testing the idea that generality can reside in the model‑building agent rather than the model itself.
stories.why_it_matters: If LLM agents can reliably create task‑specific PHM models, it reduces the need for hand‑crafted, general‑purpose models and could speed up deployment on unseen equipment, improving reliability and maintenance scheduling in industry. The benchmark provides a realistic test of this approach.

stories.headline: Agentic Multiverse Analysis framework deploys 150 autonomous AI agents to expose sensitivity of empirical conclusions

sources.title: When AI Analysts Disagree: Agentic Multiverse Analysis and the Robustness of Empirical Research

stories.what_happened: The paper introduces an Agentic Multiverse Analysis (AMA) framework that makes the impact of dozens of analytical choices (“forks”) visible at scale. In a pilot study the authors deployed 150 autonomous AI coding agents to run variations of a single observational dataset and a set of research questions, demonstrating how the framework can systematically explore how conclusions change with different methodological decisions.
stories.why_it_matters: By automating large‑scale multiverse analyses, AMA reveals how robust—or fragile—empirical findings are to hidden analytical decisions, addressing a key reproducibility concern in data‑driven research. This transparency can improve confidence in results and guide more informed methodological choices.
